stories.title: Dr Farooq Abdullah dismisses reports of NC split, says legislators' grievances genuine
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 06: National Conference president Farooq Abdullah on Friday dismissed reports of a possible split in the party as baseless, saying the concerns raised by around 16 legislators were genuine and would be addressed by the leadership. Speaking to reporters, after meeting the legislators, Dr Abdullah said the party leadership had listened to their grievances and would take steps to resolve them. "We have spoken to them. Their problems were genuine and they were heard properly. We will take some steps quickly and some steps slowly," he said. He said the party would work towards strengthening both the organisation and the government to ensure that people's problems were addressed. Dismissing speculation about a possible rebellion within the ruling party, Abdullah said the National Conference remained united and could not be divided. "The news that a split is taking place in the National Conference is completely baseless. This community is organised, and those who think they can break it should remember that it has never been broken and never will be," he said. The meeting comes amid reports of discontent among a section of NC legislators over the functioning of the party and the government. Around 16 MLAs had sought an interaction with the party leadership, triggering speculation about internal differences within the ruling party. Dr Farooq Abdullah also reiterated the party's commitment to seeking restoration of Jammu and Kashmir's statehood and Article 370. "Our fight for the restoration of statehood will continue. Our fight for Article 370 and Article 35A will also continue, and, God willing, we will take the matter to the Supreme Court," he said. The National Conference had made restoration of Jammu and Kashmir's special status and statehood key promises in its 2024 Assembly election manifesto. The Supreme Court had upheld the Centre's August 2019 decision to abrogate Article 370 in December 2023, while directing that Assembly elections be held in Jammu and Kashmir and statehood be restored at the earliest. The NC-led government, headed by Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, assumed office in October 2024 after the party emerged as the single largest party in the Assembly elections. (KNS)

article_sentences: A bench of Justices PS Narasimha and R Mahadevan also gave the government two more months to implement the ruling, beyond the six months granted in March.

The Supreme Court on Friday reaffirmed that a parent’s salary from a public sector undertaking or private-sector job cannot alone determine whether a candidate falls within the OBC creamy layer and is excluded from reservation.

Rejecting the Centre’s request to apply its March 11, 2026 verdict only to future cases, the court said the candidates before it were entitled to reservation benefits and consequential placement and allotment of posts.
It clarified, however, that completed selections, appointments, seniority and promotions would not be reopened.

In the Union of India vs Rohith Nathan case, the court had ruled that creamy-layer status could not be determined solely by a parent’s salary or employment income from a public sector undertaking or private firm.
Under the 1993 office memorandum, the status and category of the parent’s post must be considered along with the prescribed income or wealth test.

Reaffirming that ruling, the bench said the candidates involved in the case fell within the OBC non-creamy layer and were entitled to reservation benefits in the selection processes in which they had participated.

The Centre had asked the court to invoke Article 142 of the Constitution to give the verdict prospective effect, arguing that applying it to past and ongoing recruitment could affect people who were not parties to the case and cause “complete administrative chaos”.
The court found “no convincing or reasonable justification” to defer implementation.
It said granting relief to the candidates before it would not affect anyone else’s seniority or reopen completed selections and appointments.

The bench also referred to a December 20, 2016 letter from the Department of Personnel and Training, which had clarified that selections through the Civil Services Examination, 2016 were subject to the outcome of the pending appeals.
The court said claims by similarly placed people whose cases were pending before courts, tribunals or other competent authorities could be decided on their individual merits.

The pending cases will be decided by the courts on their own merits and entitlement.

The Applicant therefore respectfully submits that the temporal operation of the Judgment requires clarification so as to avoid unsettling completed selections, appointments and admissions and the consequential rights arising therefrom”, the plea states.

The Centre had sought two years to establish equivalence of posts in other organisations with government posts after consultations with the concerned stakeholders and to formulate a uniform mechanism for determining OBC creamy-layer status where equivalence has not been established.

The Centre had also sought permission to finalise service allocation for 958 candidates recommended by the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) in the Civil Services Examination (CSE) 2025, pending a decision on the clarification application.

stories.summary: The growing chatter around a potential cut in equity long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax has shifted attention to a deeper market debate among investors—whether India is trying to attract foreign investors with tax incentives at a time its valuations remain a hurdle. While a friendlier tax regime could improve returns at the margin, many investors argue that foreign institutional investors (FIIs) allocations are driven far more by earnings prospects and relative valuations.“No tax change has turned a falling market. Removal would raise the response of flows to a rising market, not create the rise,” says Venkatesh Balasubramaniam, managing director and head of research, JM Financial. He insists that lower taxes are not enough to attract more foreign investors to India. “Tax matters at the margin and as a signal, but it cannot by itself bring FIIs back,” he says further, adding that tax relief could fetch an estimated $3–5 billion in foreign institutional investors (FIIs) inflows by FY28.India taxes FIIs like any other category of investors—at 20 percent on short-term gains and 12.5 percent on long-term gains—while most Asian markets impose no capital gains tax at all. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has recommended removing LTCG tax for FIIs and easing tax treatment for mutual fund scheme switches, though the final decision rests with the Centre, a Reuters report said. The proposals come amid continued foreign outflows from Indian equities and follow discussions in which overseas investors flagged taxation as a key concern.Also Read: Indian stock market running on oppressed, caged capitalFIIs have been consistently dumping Indian stocks over the last few months, so much so that only domestic institutional investors (DIIs), including mutual funds, banks and pension funds, have provided valuable support to the overall markets.In October, FIIs sold $2.2 billion worth of equities taking their net outflows for the year to $30.4 billion. DIIs, meanwhile, remained net buyers, investing $6.3 billion in October, taking their cumulative equity inflows to $74.1 billion in the year so far.Meanwhile, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said at a media event that the government is mindful of investor concerns over high valuations and capital gains taxes but cautioned that tax incentives alone do not drive market performance. However, when analysing recent FPI outflows, it is helpful to view the headline tax rate as one component of a broader macroeconomic and regulatory ecosystem, rather than the singular driver of capital movement.“Historically, while taxes are a critical consideration for foreign allocators, they do not act in isolation. Several mature global markets command premium capital despite carrying a high combined capital gains tax burden. This may indicate that global investors can comfortably absorb local taxes if the broader investment landscape remains compelling,” Lohia says.According to him, to build on the positive intent behind rationalising LTCG tax, policymakers must also focus on creating an environment of sustained regulatory and tax certainty.“Continuing to reinforce established international tax principles—such as acknowledging the sufficiency of Tax Residency Certificates (TRCs) for treaty eligibility—and focusing on further accelerating dispute resolution timelines will significantly elevate investor confidence,” Lohia adds.Also Read: Ashishkumar Chauhan: The man who transformed the marketsAnalysts at Jefferies say the government needs to balance the potential fiscal impact even as the path towards converging taxation across asset classes continues. “Better FII sentiment can support both equities and the rupee, given the positioning,” they say.Following the recent tax relief for foreign investors in government securities (G-Secs), debt FII inflows picked up during June-July, reaching $9 billion. In Q1FY27, despite India’s GDP growing 7.8 percent year-on-year, FIIs sold $13.4 billion worth of equities. Earnings growth, meanwhile, is recovering with earnings per share (EPS) increasing 12.9 percent in Q1FY27, and expected to rise further to 20.6 percent in Q2FY27. But this has not marked a turnaround for FII flows.His analysis suggests that Brent crude prices have no consistent links to foreign liquidity flows over the entire period. article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (November 6) admitted for hearing plea by DMK candidate KR Periakaruppan challenging victory of TVK's Seenivasa Sethupathi by one vote in Tirupattur Constituency in the recent Tamil Nadu Assembly Elections.
A bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Aparesh Singh allowed Sethupathi to file his reply and directed that all relevant record relating to the election be preserved.
The Court admitted Periakaruppan's appeal against Madras High Court order rejecting his Election Petition against Sethupati's election.

Periakaruppan has alleged that postal votes that should have been sent to No. 158 Tiruppattur assembly constituency were wrongly sent to No. 50 Tiruppattur constituency due to a similar constituency name and were subsequently rejected.
He alleged that instead of rejecting the postal votes, they should have been sent to the correct constituency and counted.
He submitted that if such postal votes were counted for No. 158 Tiruppattur constituency, the one-vote margin would not have occurred and Periakaruppan would have received a majority.
He thus argued that the election procedures were not followed as per law.
Sethupathi thus argued that there was no material fact to show how the rules were violated, in a manner which could materially affect the election and/or its outcome.
It was also argued that there was no basis for the allegation for exactly one postal ballot to have been received elsewhere in a similarly named constituency.
Sethupathi also argued that Periakaruppan's objections with respect to irregularity in counting of votes was raised belatedly after the declaration of results.
It was argued that no such objection was raised at the time of counting of votes.
Thus, it was argued that the objection was made only as a ruse to file the election petition.

article_sentences: It is particularly unfortunate that a dispute remained pending for several decades, the Court commented.

The Supreme Court on Friday directed the States of Punjab and Haryana to supply approximately 11,973 million units (MU) of electricity to Himachal Pradesh over a period of 20 years, thereby bringing to a close a decades-long dispute over the sharing of power generated from the Bhakra-Nangal and Beas hydroelectric projects.

A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana directed the two States to supply the power arrears at the rate of approximately 598 million units per annum during the lean seasons (October to March).
The Court also directed that Himachal Pradesh's liability towards its 7.19% share of the capital cost of the projects, assessed at ₹420.77 crores, be adjusted against the energy arrears.
For this purpose, the electricity shall be valued at ₹3.85 per unit, resulting in an adjustment of approximately 1,093 million units.

The directions were issued in a suit instituted by Himachal Pradesh in 1996 under Article 131 of the Constitution, seeking its rightful share in the electricity generated from the two hydroelectric projects.
The Court had, in its 2011 judgment, declared Himachal Pradesh entitled to 7.19% of the power attributable to the erstwhile composite State of Punjab.
However, the implementation of the decree led to further disputes concerning the quantum of arrears, the applicable tariff and the capital-cost liabilities of the States.
The Union of India had computed Himachal Pradesh's total energy arrears at 13,066 million units for the period from November 1, 1966, until October 2011.
It proposed that the arrears be supplied in kind over 15 years, with the capital-cost liability being adjusted against the energy entitlement.

Punjab disputed the computation, contending that the arrears should be reduced after accounting for the additional power supplied to Himachal Pradesh and that the capital-cost liability should be calculated differently.
Haryana also raised objections concerning the quantum of its liability.

stories.headline: Tanvi Patri becomes first Indian to win youth olympics singles silver
stories.title: Tanvi Patri becomes first Indian to win youth olympics singles silver
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 6: Tanvi Patri's historic run in the 2026 Summer Youth Olympics culminated in her becoming the first Indian women's singles badminton player to clinch a silver medal after she went down against reigning World Junior Champion Zhang Yi Xin in a nail-biting summit clash in Dakar, Senegal, on Thursday. Tanvi saved six match points and missed three of her own to go down 15-21, 21-13, 26-24 in an hour and 22 minutes in a gold medal clash that kept everyone watching live action on the edge of their seats. On Wednesday, Tanvi had become the first Indian female player to reach the final of the badminton discipline in the Youth Olympics. Before Tanvi, HS Prannoy (2010) and Lakshya Sen (2018) had won individual silver medals in the Youth Olympic Games. Sen had also bagged the mixed team gold with Team Alpha, which included shuttlers from eight different countries. In the gold medal match on Thursday, Tanvi took her time to get going in the opening game before she claimed seven straight points to go from 3-5 to 10-5. The Indian created many openings with her punch tosses and controlled the net brilliantly to then bag the opening game in 25 minutes. She began the second game by taking a 4-0 lead before the drift coming from behind her started to affect Tanvi’s control on the clears, and Zhang took control of the game after the mid-game interval to force a decider. Zhang then took control of the decider early with her trademark cross-court drops to open up a 19-10 lead. Tanvi fought back to close the gap to four points at 19-15, but an error on a cross-court smash from the Indian handed her opponent five match points. Tanvi saved those five match points and had three chances of wrapping the gold medal. But it was the experience of Zhang that ultimately made the difference. Applauding Tanvi’s dream run in the Dakar Youth Olympics, Badminton Association of India General Secretary said, “Tanvi Patri has made the entire nation proud with a historic achievement at the Youth Olympic Games. Winning a silver medal at just 15 is an extraordinary accomplishment and a moment of immense pride for India. “Her fighting spirit, composure, and performances throughout the competition reflect the immense potential of our young sporting generation. This achievement is a significant milestone for Indian sport and a testament to the growing presence of our athletes on the global stage. On behalf of the Badminton Association of India and its member colleagues, I congratulate Tanvi and everyone who has supported her journey,” he added. --IANS

stories.title: Rajasthan to appoint 235 athletes to govt jobs, 9 as DSPs
stories.summary: Jaipur, Nov 6: In a major boost to sportspersons in Rajasthan, the Chief Minister Bhajanlal Sharma government has approved out-of-turn government appointments for 235 medal-winning athletes, including 73 para-athletes. Nine of them will be appointed as Deputy Superintendents of Police (DSPs), while the others will be recruited to various government departments. The decision was taken at the seventh meeting of the state-level committee, chaired by Chief Secretary V. Srinivas at the Government Secretariat. The committee reviewed 286 applications submitted by general and para-athletes and approved appointment proposals for 235 candidates. The appointments are intended to recognise the achievements of athletes who have won medals at national and international sporting events and provide them with government employment in recognition of their performances. The approved appointments have been divided into three categories. Under Category A, nine athletes have been selected for appointment as DSPs. Under Category B, two athletes will be appointed to the Excise Department, one as a Patrolling Officer and the other as a Sub-Inspector. The largest number of appointments falls under Category C, with 224 athletes set to join various government departments. These appointments will include positions such as Clerk Grade-II, Constable, Excise Constable, Excise Guard and Deputy Jailor. Significantly, the Category C list includes 73 para-athletes, ensuring that sportspersons who have excelled in para-sports also benefit from the government's employment initiative. The Rajasthan government has already provided out-of-turn government appointments to 187 medal-winning athletes since December 2023. With the approval of 235 additional appointment proposals, the initiative is expected to gain further momentum. The policy aims to encourage sporting excellence by offering employment opportunities to athletes in recognition of their achievements at national and international competitions. The committee also reviewed issues concerning athletes already employed in the Forest Department. Officials discussed difficulties faced by these sportspersons during their service and examined an action plan to address their concerns. Proposals were also considered to provide a one-time relaxation in service rules to facilitate their adjustment in other departments, wherever required. The proposed measures are expected to provide relief to athletes currently serving in the Forest Department and help ensure better utilisation of their sporting achievements and professional capabilities. --IANS

stories.title: High Court rejects plea by two IAS officers in arms licence scam PIL, seeks report on prosecution sanction
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 06: The Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh High Court has rejected an application by two IAS officers seeking intervention in the long-pending Arms Licences Scam PIL and a direction to the Centre to consider their representations before deciding on a proposal for grant of prosecution sanction against them. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Dr Pushpendra Singh Bhati and Justice Rajnesh Oswal observed that there was no justification for issuing such a direction, noting that the officers' plea appeared to suggest that the authorities would not apply their minds properly without the court's intervention. The application was filed by Pandurang Kondbaroa Pole, a 2004-batch AGMUT cadre IAS officer currently posted as Secretary, Land and Building, Government of NCT of Delhi, and Shahid Iqbal Choudhary, a 2009-batch AGMUT cadre officer presently posted as Secretary, Government of Arunachal Pradesh. The officers had sought impleadment in PIL No. 9/2012, titled Sheikh Mohd. Shafi and Another versus Union of India and Others. They had also sought a direction to the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) to consider their representations before taking a decision on the CBI's proposal for grant of prosecution sanction. Appearing for the officers, Senior Advocate Sakal Bhushan, assisted by Advocate Rahul Sharma, argued that the doctrine of deemed sanction could not be applied mechanically and that the matter required a case-specific assessment by the competent authorities and the court. He submitted that the officers were only seeking consideration of their representations before a decision was taken on the prosecution sanction proposal. The Bench, however, declined to grant the relief sought. “The reason why this Court has not accepted the application is that merely the gist of the submission made by learned Senior counsel was that unless the Court directs there will not be proper application of mind by the respondents, which does not seem to find any favour of the Court,” the Bench observed. Bhushan subsequently sought permission to withdraw the application and pursue the representations before the DoPT. The court accordingly dismissed the application as withdrawn, observing that the officers did not require its permission to pursue appropriate remedies available under law. During the hearing, Advocate S.S. Ahmed, appearing for the PIL petitioners, informed the court that the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) had submitted an updated status report in compliance with its July 6, 2026 order. According to Ahmed, the MHA had stated that, following detailed examination and consultations with the investigating agency and the Jammu and Kashmir Government, it had finalised its views and comments on the proposal and forwarded its considered opinion to the DoPT for a final decision under the prescribed procedure. Ahmed sought a direction to the DoPT to place its final decision before the court. Taking note of the submission, the Division Bench directed Deputy Solicitor General of India Vishal Sharma, appearing for the Union Government, to submit a comprehensive report detailing compliance with the court's orders passed from time to time. The PIL has been listed for further hearing on December 23, 2026. (KNT)
